 2026 Fantasy Football Week 11 Defense (DST) Rankings and Streamers 
 By
 Eric Samulski , 
 By
 Eric Samulski 
     Published November 17, 2026 10:51 AM 
 Add 
 on Google 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Email
 Add 
 on Google 
 Overall, I had a fine week in the picks. I hit on five of my top 10 defenses and 13 of my top 16. The consensus rankings at Fantasy Pros hit on the same 5 of 10 but had 14 of the top 16. My average miss was by 6.2 spots, and the consensus was 6.6, so I was pretty much on par with the consensus ranks this week. Not great, but not an awful showing, and I’m still hitting at a higher rate than consensus on the season. 
 I had some success with the Colts, Vikings, and Rams, who were all ranked higher than consensus. The Vikings were the top-ranked defense, the Rams were second, and the Colts finished in the top five with 12 fantasy points. The top-12 ranking for the Dolphins also paid off, so there were some good calls that, again, show us that the matchup has been carrying a lot of signal these days. With some teams (Cardinals, Colts, Dolphins) bottoming out, there are a lot of matchups that we want to aggressively target with our defenses. 
 However, some of the chalk picks really failed in Week 10. The Jaguars, Ravens, and Texans all finished with under seven fantasy points. Of that group, only the Jaguars have been a strong fantasy defense this week, so maybe we attacked the Chargers and Browns, who are now only kinda bad offenses in the larger landscape, with two defenses that are also not great. Of course, injuries for the Texans’ defense played a role, but we’re probably at the stage where we just trust the best overall defenses to keep delivering over hunting for “easy matchups.”

 Chart data Top-10 hits Top-10 hit rate Top-16 hits Top-16 hit rate 
 My Ranks, Week 10 5 50.0% 13 81% 
 Consensus, Week 10 5 50.0% 14 88% 
 My Ranks, season to date 53 53% 108 66% 
 Consensus*, season to date 48 48% 99 59% 
 *Consensus Rankings are taken from FantasyPros Consensus Rankings around 10 am on Sundays. For Week 1 only this season, I used a combination of ClutchPoints and RotoBaller. 
 BOD Formula and Philosophy 
 If you’ve read my earlier articles, then you know that I value defenses that get pressure on the quarterback and create turnover opportunities, which is likely what most people value. However, that means I look at underlying metrics and try to value the quality of the defense over simply saying, “Who is playing a bad offense?” Yet, when I did a deep dive this offseason, I discovered that the stats most commonly associated with top-10 fantasy defenses were first-down allowed, points per game allowed, and third-down conversion rate allowed. So even though I love defenses who get pressure, defenses who can also get off the field quickly tend to be the best fantasy defenses. Perhaps this isn’t a shock, but maybe we’re not really paying attention to the relevant stats when predicting fantasy defensive performance.
 The next four most predictive defensive stats were pressure rate, passes defended, turnover rate, and explosive play rate allowed (plays over 20+ yards). With that in mind, I decided to update my Best Overall Defense (BOD) formula to include just these seven stats. I doubled the weight of the first three stats, which are more predictive, and have a single weight for the other four stats. I also incorporate Vegas’ implied team total in the algorithm every week, and when we get opponent stats, I will include fantasy points allowed to opposing defenses as part of the equation since fantasy points are the strongest predictor of fantasy points.
 I’ll obviously have to adjust the algorithm each week for injuries or weather, but I try not to rely too much on “gut feel” or concerns about wind, etc.
 With that out of the way, onto the rankings.
 FOR A MORE DETAILED DISCUSSION OF DST PLAYS FOR THIS WEEK, CHECK OUT ERIC’S PICK 3(DST) VIDEO OVER ON THE NFL ON NBC YOUTUBE PAGE. 
 2026 Week 11 DST Rankings 
 Rank Tier One DSTs Opponent BOD RANKING 
 1 Kansas City Chiefs vs ARI 9 
 2 Buffalo Bills vs MIA 12 
 The Chiefs delivered for us this past Sunday against the Falcons, and I expect no different this week against an Arizona offense that looks to be a total mess. Carson Beck made his first NFL start this weekend and threw two interceptions while completing just 11 passes. Now, some of that is because his top four wide receivers are hurt, but that’s also another key reason why we want to use the Chiefs defense. On the season, the Chiefs rank 3rd in the NFL in points per game allowed, 9th in explosive play rate, 10th in third-down conversion rate, and 11th in turnover rate. Over the last six weeks, they are 5th in fantasy points scored with eight per game. Meanwhile, the Cardinals have an implied team total of just 12.5 points, which is the lowest on the slate. They also rank 21st in turnover rate, so this Chiefs defense could feast. 
 The Bills are favored by more points than any team in the NFL has been this season, and they’re favored by more points than they’ve been since back in the 2021 season. Obviously a big reason for that is that they are taking on a Dolphins team that has an implied team total of just 14.5 points, which is the second lowest on the slate. The Dolphins got decent production from Kyle McCord in his first NFL start, but he throws a lot of turnover-worthy passes. The Dolphins have the fourth-highest sack rate allowed and the 11th-highest turnover rate, so this is a prime matchup for a Bills defense that ranks fourth in fantasy points over the last six weeks with 8.8 per game. 
 Rank Tier Two DSTs Opponent BOD RANKING 
 3 Denver Broncos vs LV 11 
 4 Houston Texans vs IND 18 
 5 Pittsburgh Steelers at PHI 7 
 6 Jacksonville Jaguars at NYG 3 
 7 Chicago Bears vs NO 8 
 The Broncos are coming off a bye and into a good spot against a Las Vegas team that may be without Brock Bowers , who left Sunday’s game with an ankle injury. On the season, Denver ranks 9th in points per game allowed but isn’t top 12 in any of the other metrics that I use. However, they are a fringe top 10 defense in my rankings and are the 11th-best defense in fantasy over the last six games. So the reason I have them ranked this highly is that Las Vegas has an implied team total of 15.25 points, which is the 3rd-lowest on the slate. Fernando Mendoza took six sacks on Sunday and threw for only 143 yards without Bowers. If Bowers does play, the Broncos may move down a couple spots, but they’ll stay in this tier. 
 The Texans let us down in a pretty good matchup against the Browns this past Sunday, but this matchup against the Colts is even better. Indianapolis has the 4th-lowest implied total on the slate at 16 points, and they have the 3rd-highest turnover rate on offense and 13th-highest sack rate allowed. Daniel Jones passed for just 108 yards against the Dolphins on Sunday, and I don’t think the Colts are gonna be able to run the ball as effectively against the Texans. The Texans have not been a great defense this season, but they are second in sack rate and could be disruptive again if they get back Danielle Hunter and Azeez Al-Shaair , who both missed Sunday’s game.
 The Steelers didn’t deliver against the Bengals, but this is an entirely different situation against the Eagles. Philadelphia has the 5th-lowest implied total of the week at 17 points, and they have the 7th-highest sack rate allowed on the season. Now, the Eagles are coming off a bye, so it’s unclear if they will get DeVonta Smith or Dontayvion Wicks back, which means we need to monitor that situation, but I have no problem playing a defense against Joe Milton . On the season, Pittsburgh ranks 4th in explosive play rate, 7th in points per game allowed, 7th in third-down conversion rate, 9th in sack rate, and 10th in turnover rate. They’re averaging 7.0 fantasy points per game over the last six weeks, and I like them this week if the Eagles remain short-handed. 
 Oh, look, another team that didn’t deliver on Sunday with the Jags putting up just three fantasy points against the Titans. Still, on the season, Jacksonville ranks 2nd in points per game allowed, 3rd in turnover rate, 6th in third-down conversion rate, and 12th in explosive play rate. That has led to 7.4 fantasy points per game over the last six weeks, which is a solid enough total. The Giants have the 9th-lowest implied total at 20.25 points and are 9th-highest in sack rate allowed and 13th-highest in turnover rate, so it’s a solid enough matchup. The Jags should also get Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux on the field for the first time this week, which is a nice boost for this defense. 
 The Bears come off the bye into a good matchup against a Saints offense that has been struggling of late and just lost two starting offensive linemen in Taliese Fuaga and Erik McCoy . Fuaga’s backup, Asim Richards , is also out, so the Saints will be using a third-string right tackle to block Montez Sweat . That’s gonna be a problem. It’s also part of the reason the Saints have an implied team total of just 19 points on Sunday. On the season, Chicago ranks 1st in third-down conversion rate, 3rd in sack rate, and 8th in points per game allowed, so I’m expecting a strong showing here. 
 Rank Tier Three DSTs Opponent BOD RANKING 
 8 Los Angeles Chargers vs NYJ 21 
 9 Minnesota Vikings at SF 1 
 10 San Francisco 49ers vs MIN 10 
 11 Detroit Lions vs TB 16 
 12 New York Jets at LAC 19 
 13 Carolina Panthers vs BAL 26 
 The Chargers could see a Jets offense without Geno Smith , which would mean rookie Cade Klubnik would get the start under center. Klubnik looked solid enough in relief of Geno, and he will avoid more sacks than Geno does, but he’ll also throw more turnover-worthy passes. The Jets have the 6th-lowest implied total at 18.75 points and have the 5th-highest sack rate allowed, but Klubnik could improve on some of that. The Chargers are not a great defense and are averaging just 3.2 fantasy points per game over the last six weeks, so I can’t get too excited.
 Look, this is a terrible matchup for the Vikings, but they are clearly the best defense in the NFL, and so they have an argument to be startable every single week. Especially after they just dominated the Packers on Sunday. On the season, Minnesota ranks 1st in points per game allowed, 1st in sack rate, 3rd in third-down conversion rate, 4th in turnover rate, and 6th in explosive play rate. They’re averaging 10.8 fantasy points per game over the last six weeks, and I think they could still put up 6-8 points here against the 49ers. Injuries to Mike Evans and Trent Williams will play a role in where I ultimately rank the Vikings. 
 On the other hand, you could maybe talk yourself into the 49ers defense this week, even though Kirk Cousins has made this Vikings offense look much better. Minnesota has the 12th-lowest implied total at 21.75 points and has the 6th-highest sack rate allowed, which won’t improve too much with Cousins under center. On the season, San Francisco ranks 2nd in explosive play rate, 7th in turnover rate, and 11th in points per game allowed. That has led to 8.0 fantasy points per game over the last six weeks, so I think I can talk myself into the 49ers here. 
 It’s hard to feel good about rostering a Lions defense that won’t have Aidan Hutchinson and might not have D.J. Reed either, but there are six teams on bye and a lot of bad defenses, so there will be some tough calls to make this week. On the season, Detroit is sack rate 4th, but obviously Hutchinson is a huge part of that success. Tampa Bay does have the third-highest sack rate allowed in the NFL, so I think the Lions could still get home for a few sacks here, but not as many as they might have if Hutchinson was healthy. Tampa Bay also has the 8th-lowest implied total at 20 points, so I think the Lions could still produce a fine enough effort. 
 The Jets gave up 31 points to the Bills, but they played a solid game against a much better offense than they’ll see this weekend. Yes, the Chargers looked fine in a win over the Ravens, but they have an implied team total of just 21.75 points, and they have the 2nd-highest sack rate allowed and highest offensive turnover rate on the season, so there are some chances for the Jets to make plays here. The Jets themselves rank 10th in explosive play rate allowed and 12th in sack rate, and I think they could be a sneaky play with the Chargers’ offensive line banged up and Ladd McConkey potentially out for another game with a back injury. 
 The Ravens offense still looked fairly average on Monday night with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback. They have an implied team total of 20.5 points, which is the 10th-lowest on the slate. They also have the 8th-highest sack rate allowed, which isn’t going to get better with immobile Brissett under center. The Panthers rank third in explosive play rate allowed, so if they can prevent big plays and get a couple sacks, they could put up a solid floor performance. 
 Rank Tier Four DSTs Opponent BOD RANKING 
 14 Cincinnati Bengals at WAS 15 
 15 Baltimore Ravens at CAR 22 
 16 Philadelphia Eagles vs PIT 31 
 17 Tampa Bay Bucs at DET 2 
 18 Dallas Cowboys vs TEN 32 
 Defenses ranked this low may be intriguing, but I can’t consider playing them outside of the deepest formats.
 The Bengals are a solid defense, ranking 7th in sack rate, 9th in turnover rate, and 10th in points per game allowed on the season. Yet, this matchup against the Commanders is not a great one, even without Terry McLaurin. Washington has an implied total of 23 points, but they are also middle of the pack in sack rate allowed and have the third-best turnover rate in the NFL on offense. I think the Bengals could maybe keep them to 20-24 points, but I don’t see a ton of other upside here. 
 Baltimore really let us down in a good matchup against the Chargers. Over the last six weeks, they’re averaging just 2.7 fantasy points per game. On the season, they rank 11th in third-down conversion rate but no other stat in the top 12 in my model. Carolina will give up pressure and sacks, but I’m just not sure the Ravens are the defense to take advantage of that. Combine that with the fact that the Panthers have an implied team total of 23 points, and this feels like a spot I’d like to avoid. 
 I love adding the Bucs this week, but I just want to keep them on my bench. The Bucs are my 2 nd -ranked defense in my season-long rankings, and they get the Panthers, Chargers, Ravens, Saints, and Falcons in their 5 games after this week. I love that. But I don’t love a matchup this weekend against a Lions team that has an implied team total of 26.5 points. The Lions are 5 th -best in the NFL in turnover rate and are middle of the pack in sack rate allowed. I just don’t see a path to lots of production for the Bucs this weekend.

 19 New York Giants vs JAX 17 
 20 Las Vegas Raiders at DEN 25 
 21 Washington Commanders vs CIN 14 
 22 Indianapolis Colts at HOU 29

 28 Green Bay Packers BYE 5
